newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: SOCCER-CAMEROON SPOIL POSSIBLE NAMIBIAN FAIRYTALE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CAMEROON SPOIL POSSIBLE NAMIBIAN FAIRYTALE.

text.p: Cameroon spoilt Namibia's Cinderella story on Saturday with a 1-0 win in their African Nations Cup qualifier in Windhoek to go within one point of qualifying for the finals in Burkina Faso next year.
Substitute Joseph Tchango volleyed the winner in the 69th minute, driving home a cross from French-based striker Patrick Suffo,
The win means Cameroon are top of the standings in group five and now need just a home draw against Kenya on July 27 to ensure a place in the 16-team tournament next February.
Namibia, who have been the surprise package of African football this year, can still qualify in second place but will need a result away in Gabon on the same day.

Namibia would have qualified had they won on Saturday but ran into a well-drilled and physically superior Cameroonian side, packed with foreign-based professionals, in a bruising encounter with few clear-cut scoring opportunities.
"They were stronger and better than us. They deserved to win," said Namibian midfielder Ricardo Mannetti.

But Namibia did have a few chances before Tchango's goal wih striker Gervatius Uri Khob seeing a fierce free kick blocked by Cameroonian captain Jacques Songo'o and Eliphas Shivute missing with a close-in header.
The home team also launched a late flurry of attacks after Cameroon defender Pierre Nlend Wome was sent off in the 82nd minute for a second bookable offence but ran into stubborn resistance.

"It was very difficult but we are back at the top of the group. We used a lot of youngsters but they played very well," said new coach Jean-Manga Onguene. "It was my first game and very important to win."

Namibia - 1-Fillemon Kanalelo; 2-Petrus Haraseb, 5-Bimbo Tjihero, 14-Stanley Gogoaseb; 4-Frans Ananias (11-Razundara Tjikuzu 71st minute), 7-Sandro de Gouveia, 10-Ricardo Mannetti, 6-Silvester Goraseb (15-Johannes Hindjou 60th), 12-Robert Nauseb; 3-Elphas Shivute, 8-Gervatius Uri Khob.

Cameroon - 1-Jacques Songo'o; 5-Simon Moukoko, 4-Ernest Oben Etchi, 6-Geremi Njitap, 8-Romarin Billong; 2-Louis Abderrahman, 3-Pierre Nlend Wome, 7-Guy Tapoko (14-Joseph Tchango 58th), 12-Fabrice Moreau; 9-Elie Bayamba (11-Vincent Kom 77th), 10-Patric Suffo.
